flows.name: keychain-secrets
flows.description: Read, write and delete the secret of a connection. No network. A secret never goes in an argument, a URL, a log or a repository file.

flows.name: code-host-api
flows.description: List and read pull requests, CI status and repositories. Create a private repository when the person clicks Create in the project creator. On each sync tick, read the CI status of the open pull requests of the person (one call each) for the checks notice. A write (open a pull request, push, comment) waits for the automation switch or a click. The team join request pushes a branch and opens a pull request after a click.

flows.name: git-remote
flows.description: Clone, fetch, pull and push with the git command and git2. Credential helpers of the person apply.

flows.name: browser-sign-in
flows.description: OAuth device flow. GitHub: /login/device/code and /login/oauth/access_token. GitLab: /oauth/authorize_device and /oauth/token, also the token refresh. The token goes to the keychain.

flows.name: issue-tracker-api
flows.description: Sync tick: read work items and comments updated since the last good poll, every 60 s by default (30 s at least). Jira /rest/api/2, GitHub api.github.com, GitLab /api/v4, Azure DevOps /_apis, Linear api.linear.app/graphql. A write (claim stamp, transition, comment, starter issue on Create issues) waits for the automation switch or a click. A worklog (send on save of a time entry, change, delete) goes out on that click only; Read the month reads the worklogs of the tickets of the month.

flows.name: model-provider-chat
flows.protocol: HTTPS, or HTTP on a local host
flows.description: GET /models and POST /chat/completions. The provider has no tools and never edits a repository.

flows.name: mcp-server-http
flows.description: The one Shipyard MCP endpoint proxies the tools of each active MCP server as <server-id>__<tool>. GitLab tools: https://<host>/api/v4/mcp.

flows.name: agent-cli-start
flows.description: Headless run with streamed JSON, or an assistant turn. The CLI calls its own vendor service: Shipyard does not proxy or control that traffic.

flows.name: mcp-loopback
flows.description: POST /mcp with the bearer token of one run. The server checks the Host and Origin headers, caps a body at 1 MiB and serves 32 requests at most at once. Another path answers 404, another method 405.

flows.name: update-check
flows.description: GET api.github.com/repos/me-cedric/Shipyard/releases/latest with no credential. It tells the person that a newer version exists. It never downloads and never installs. The address and the automatic check are preferences.

flows.name: drawio-embed
flows.description: The only network frame origin that the content security policy allows (ADR 0015): https://embed.diagrams.net. The deck frame (deck:, ADR 0016) is local. Messages are accepted from this origin only. Offline, or without an answer in 15 s, the board shows read-only.

flows.name: figma-api
flows.description: GET api.figma.com/v1 for files, thumbnails and variables, with a token from the keychain.

flows.name: openspec-validator
flows.description: The OpenSpec check runs npx with the registry https://registry.npmjs.org/ and the fixed version @fission-ai/openspec@1.15.0, so a repository .npmrc cannot redirect it. No answer in 120 s gives the finding validator missing.

flows.name: openrouter-sign-in
flows.description: OAuth PKCE. The browser opens https://openrouter.ai/auth with a code challenge and a localhost callback. Then POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/keys with the code and the verifier gives a key for the keychain. A code lasts 10 minutes.

flows.name: microsoft-login
flows.description: Deferred (Q-132): no code makes this call yet. Entra ID device code: POST login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/devicecode, then poll /token. Scope https://ai.azure.com/.default. The tokens go to the keychain.

flows.name: local-runtime-probe
flows.description: GET /api/tags on Ollama (11434), GET /v1/models on LM Studio (1234), vLLM (8000) and LiteLLM (4000). Localhost only. No other host is probed.

flows.name: any-other-destination
flows.description: Shipyard itself calls no other host. A child process that it starts (an agent CLI, an MCP server started with npx or uvx) makes its own calls. Redirects are never followed, so a credential cannot reach a second host.
